problem: Existing VLN methods turn raw images into visual tokens or implicit features, which requires large-scale visual pre-training and large (>=7B) models, and generalizes poorly under changes in lighting, texture and layout. They also leave a modality gap that stops them from fully reusing pretrained language models.
motivation: Semantic segmentation models generalize well across domains, whereas navigation models fed raw pixels overfit the appearance of their training environments. Translating observations into structured text lets a small pretrained language model do the navigation reasoning directly, with less training data and lower deployment cost.
key_idea: Convert RGB-D observations into an N×N grid of text (depth, dominant semantic class, color name per cell), concatenate it with the instruction, and have a small fine-tuned language model predict action chunks.
insight: Most of the useful navigation signal survives compression into grid text. The ablations show depth is the most critical piece (removing it drops SR from 53.6 to 21.6), followed by history (SR 26.5) and grid resolution (4×4 gives SR 34.5). A 0.6B text-only model reaches accuracy close to 7B+ VLMs that were trained on extra data, and its OS is strikingly high, while stop prediction is the weak point.
method: Structured grid observation: the RGB-D frame and its semantic map are split into an N×N grid; each cell gets mean depth, the largest-area semantic class, and an HSV-derived color name, written as '[i,j]: depth=d, semantic=s, color=c'.
Multi-resolution memory: the current frame uses a 6×6 grid, 2 short-term history frames use 4×4, and 16 long-term history frames use 2×2, each with a time-step label, ordered chronologically.
Prompt construction: a system description (action space, task, constraints), the structured observation sequence and the instruction are combined into a pure-text prompt.
Backbone with action-chunk heads: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B encodes the prompt, and 4 linear heads predict a 4-action chunk over {stop, left 15°, right 15°, forward 25cm}.
Training: LoRA fine-tuning with class-balanced weighted cross-entropy averaged over the 4 steps; LLM-augmented instructions; trained on R2R-CE and RxR-CE only.
Perception module: semantic maps come from the dataset or from SegFormer, Grounded SAM or YOLO-SAM. For the real robot, SegFormer is fine-tuned on about 1000 annotated images.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (LoRA fine-tuned) with linear action heads; SegFormer or dataset GT for semantics
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE trajectories converted to structured text, with LLM-augmented instructions; no extra datasets. Real-world: about 1000 annotated images for SegFormer plus 50 real navigation samples
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB-D converted to grid text (semantic, color, depth), plus history frames
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: stop / turn left 15° / turn right 15° / forward 25 cm, predicted as 4-step chunks
setting.privileged: Semantic segmentation maps may be taken directly from the datasets (GT semantics) rather than predicted; otherwise none

numbers.extra: trained on R2R-CE and RxR-CE only; no waypoint predictor; semantics may come from dataset annotations

numbers_note: The RxR-CE NE is inconsistent: the table prints 6.87 while the text says 6.95. The table value is used. Ablation results on R2R-CE val-unseen: 4×4 resolution gives SR 34.5, no history gives SR 26.5, no depth gives SR 21.6. Real-world results are not quantified.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen, SOL-Nav reaches SR 53.6 / SPL 49.2 / OS 72.9, beating NaVILA (49.7 SR) and other methods that use no extra data or waypoint predictor. It is slightly below ETPNav and InternVLA-N1 (SR 58.2), which use a waypoint predictor or extra data, but its OS is far higher. On RxR-CE it gets SR 48.6 / SPL 42.3 / OS 60.5, comparable to UniNaVid and NaVILA and below InternVLA-N1 (53.5 SR), with a model over 10× smaller.
limitations: Semantic, color and depth grids lose fine-grained details such as shape and texture, which hurts precise navigation in complex scenes.
Stop prediction is weak (high OS but lower SR), and performance depends on the quality of the upstream segmentation model.
Real-world evaluation is qualitative, with no quantitative results, and the reported 0.8 s latency is on a small setup with a fine-tuned SegFormer.
